title: Want Into Grandma’s Marathon? This New Option Lets 100 Runners Register Early - Duluth Country Radio
content: If you're reading this from Duluth, there is no doubt you know how big of a deal Grandma's Marathon is! People come from all over the country AND the world to take part in the race, and to watch their loved ones. It has been named a top race, holding its own against runs in major cities. That's just how special it is - and it's one of the most beautiful courses for a run, too! With that said, it can be stressful to try and get into any of the Grandma's Marathon weekend races. From the Garry Bjorklund Half Marathon to the full thing to the William A. Irvin 5K, all of the races sell out every single year. While there are options to snag a bib if you miss out, it's best to grab one of your own so you can be ready to roll. This year, Grandma's Marathon organizers are offering up a new incentive to help you skip the registration day madness. Seriously, registration can be crazy and even nerve-wrecking at times! Now, organizers have shared an alternative for avid runners who want to skip registration day all together - and it all benefits a good cause. This year, registration will be opened early for 100 runners. How can you be one of those lucky 100 runners? Make a $500 donation to the Young Athletes Foundation before October 1st. They have saved 50 spots for the half and 50 spots for the full marathon. This donation will cover the cost of your race as well and of course, the rest will help provide scholarships, equipment, registration fees and more for kids in the Twin Ports. The early registration option is in full swing as we speak - and it is first come, first serve. What else do you get? Two finish line bleacher passes for race weekend, two entries into a 2027 YAF race of your choice, a YAF hat and a discount on entry into the official Grandma's Marathon Training Group and the online store. Wow! If you are an avid runner AND want to give back to the kids in the community, you should register sooner rather than later and make your donation. You can do so right now on the official Grandma's Marathon website. Otherwise, be prepared for a hefty line when registration opens on October 1st. Good luck!

title: Rochester Man Pleads Guilty in Multiple Officer Assaults - KROC-AM
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - A Rochester man with a long history of alleged attacks on law enforcement officers has entered guilty pleas to charges in five of the cases against him. Under the terms of a plea agreement filed in Olmsted County Court, 33-year-old Mahamed Adan Abikar has admitted to four counts of felony fourth-degree assault involving law enforcement and one count of fifth-degree assault. He is scheduled to be sentenced in November. The guilty pleas stem from incidents dating back to 2022, when he was accused of kicking a Rochester police officer in the abdomen during a response to a report of a disorderly man. The following year, Abikar was charged with kicking another officer in the groin while he was allegedly resisting arrest. Abikar's cases also cover an alleged attack on a detention deputy in the Olmsted County jail in 2023 and another incident in the jail in 2024 when he was accused of spitting into the mouth of a detention deputy. His other guilty plea stems from an assault on a Rochester police officer in the downtown parking ramp last year, during which he allegedly struck the officer on the head with the bottom half of a broken cane and spit into the face of another officer. The plea deal indicates that felony charges stemming from three other incidents will be dismissed.

title: Duluth To Host 2027 IIHF U-18 World Hockey Championship - Duluth Country Radio
content: It was announced today that Duluth will be the host city for an international sporting event next year. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), in conjunction with several local and regional representatives, announced Thursday morning at AMSOIL Arena that the 2027 IIHF Under-18 Championship tournament will be coming to the Northland next spring. The IIHF hosted its World Juniors event in Minnesota at the beginning of 2026, with Duluth being one of the cities that hosted exhibition games before the tournament in the Twin Cities. During the announcement event on Thursday morning, Minnesota Sports and Entertainment President and CEO Wendy Blackshaw commented that she and her organization were "blown away" by Duluth's participation and welcoming spirit for the exhibition games. She went on to express the hope that continues with the upcoming Under-18 tournament, saying, "Let's remind the world why we are the State of Hockey", encouraging Northlanders to support the event through volunteering, attending games, and sponsorship opportunities. Duluth Mayor Roger Reinert shared remarks during the event about how Duluth has a history of hosting world-class events, pointing to Grandma's Marathon as a prime example. He says hosting the IIHF U-18 event in the Spring of 2027 will give Duluth another way to showcase the area and welcome others from around the world. Just like with Grandma's Marathon, he is inviting community members to be part of volunteer opportunities around this event and be good ambassadors for the area as visitors arrive. USA Hockey executive director Pat Kelleher commented via a written release, saying, “Duluth is one of America’s great hockey communities and an ideal setting for this tournament. Fans will have the chance to experience elite international competition and see many of the future stars of the NHL competing on a world stage for the first time.” As highlighted by USA Hockey Assistant Executive Director Tony Driscoll, NHL talent like Quinn Hughes and Matt Boldy, along with local names like Max & Victor Plante have all played in U-18 tournaments over the years. The entirety of the 2027 IIHF U-18 event will be hosted at AMSOIL Arena, with the preliminary round games getting underway on April 21. A total of 10 participating nations will be divided into two groups. Each team will play the other four teams in their group in the preliminary rounds starting April 21, with the top four teams from each group moving on to the quarterfinals on April 29, and the winners advancing to the semifinals on May 1. Group A: United States, Sweden, Latvia, Denmark, and Norway Group B: Canada, Slovakia, Finland, Belarus, and Czechia Tony Driscoll laid out the first few games for Team USA during the preliminary rounds, which include the first game on April 21 against Norway, a game against Latvia on April 23, an April 24 matchup against Sweden, and a game against Denmark on April 26. The bronze medal game and gold medal game will both be hosted on May 2, with the bronze game at AMSOIL at 1 pm, and the gold medal game at 5 pm. title: Olmsted County Declares Local Emergency After Sept. 2 Storm - 106.9 KROC
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - The Olmsted County Board has voted to declare a state of local emergency in the aftermath of the severe storm that smashed through southeastern Minnesota on September 2. According to a news release, the declaration clears the way for local jurisdictions in Olmsted County to apply for emergency assistance from the state of Minnesota. That assistance would help defray the expenses incurred in restoring power and clearing away debris from the storm. The next step in the process will be for Olmsted County Emergency Management to request a Preliminary Damage Assessment from the Minnesota Department of Public Safety's Homeland Security and Emergency Management division. If the assessment determines the damage meets the threshold set by the state, a request for a state disaster declaration will be submitted to Gov. Tim Walz. If approved, a state disaster declaration would allow the City of Rochester and other local governments to apply for funding from the Minnesota Disaster Assistance Contingency Account, which could cover up to 75% of the cost of the emergency response. The storm system produced straight-line winds of nearly 70 mph and knocked out power to thousands of homes and businesses in the Rochester area. Rochester Public Utilities General Manager Tim McCollough now says that nearly 11,000 RPU customers experienced outages as a result of the powerful storm. The City of Rochester has reported that its personnel have responded to nearly 650 storm-related tasks, which have largely involved widespread tree and limb damage. Earlier this week, Rochester officials issued a statement indicating the cleanup process could continue for another two to three weeks.

title: Scandia Marks 51 Years Of Taco Daze, The Labor Day Weekend Tradition Born From A 1975 Boy Scout Taco Sale - 98.1 - Minnesota's New Country
content: As we get ready to embrace fall officially starting next week, many town celebrations are in the books. One Minnesota city, which has a population of less than 4,000 residents, just had its yearly celebration that includes tacos and a 'running of the meatballs' which makes this 'Swedish' inspired town the place to be the weekend after Labor Day. Last Saturday, I had the chance to experience one Minnesota town festival unlike many others. The quaint city of Scandia, a few miles North of Stillwater in Washington County, hosted its 51st annual Taco Daze celebration. For a town with deep Scandinavian roots, just take a look around and note all the Dala Horse statues; the celebration seems oddly named, as you don't think about Swedish tacos. But they certainly make it work. Scandia's Taco Daze started in 1975, when the local Boy Scout troop looked for a way to fundraise and decided selling tacos was the way to do it. The whole town came together to help those kids out. Eventually, the local Lions Club took over the event, and eventually other things were added to the day, like a parade, car show, and, of course, the 'running of the meatballs'. The name of the event, the running of the meatballs, makes it sound like an actual running event, where people dress up as meatballs. However fun that sounds, that isn't what the event is. Instead, those attending the event have the opportunity to 'buy' a meatball for a chance at winning the race, and by doing so, also win some money. To me, it was similar to those rubber duck races. Sign up for the 98.1 Minnesota's New Country Newsletter Thankfully, the event doesn't use real meatballs, but they do paint golf balls brown to look like a meatball, and then send them downhill on a race course, where the winning meatball crosses the finish line at the bottom of the road. If you like to experience new things, the event is held the Saturday after Labor Day. Learn more about the event by following the celebration's social media page here.

title: TSM Myth responds after clip of Leena on his stream goes viral - Dexerto
content: Popular Twitch streamer Ali ‘Myth’ Kabbani has responded after a clip of TSM president Leena Xu went viral during his April 25 broadcast. Myth was among the first few Fortnite players signed to TSM in 2018, alongside the likes Hamlinz and Daequan, and has since gone on to build a massive fan base of over 6 million followers on his Twitch channel. During his April 25 broadcast, the popular streamer decided to entertain viewers by inviting TSM President Leena Xu to cut his hair due to the current lockdown restrictions, which resulted in hilarity for everyone involved. Towards the end of his stream, however, a clip of Leena made it’s way to Reddit, titled “Leena’s Shirt too Short” as she had a slight wardrobe malfunction, which instantly went viral. Myth responded to the post after his stream had ended, providing some context for those viewing the post and explained that it was an accident. “Leena doesn’t really stream much at all and the camera was at the wrong angle.” he admitted,” I really just want to make sure y’all don’t go assuming the wrong thing about her.” “It would be a shame if people I invite to my stream decide to never come back on for small incidents like this,” he added, calling for fans not to be harsh on Leena’s mistake. Although it is unlikely to result in a suspension for the TSM star, he has still deleted the April 25 broadcast from his channel. Yall wish u had a cut like mine, ahaa haa 🤪😉😌 pic.twitter.com/KD5xy0UQg1 However, following Alinity’s recent ban for her wardrobe malfunction, it is understandable for Myth to take precautionary measures to ensure that his channel does not receive the same punishment. title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is a No-Brainer Buy On Repeat And Not For The Reason You Think - 24/7 Wall St.

Everyone buying TSMC stock is watching the wrong number. The real reason to own shares hides one layer beneath the AI headlines, inside a bottleneck so tight that even TSMC's own customers cannot get enough of it. I keep adding shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM | TSM Price Prediction), and the reason has almost nothing to do with the AI accelerator headlines you have been reading. The reason lives one layer deeper, inside a packaging technology called Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate. The market routinely focuses on TSMC’s nanometer logic nodes (3nm, 2nm, A16), but the real choke point in modern AI accelerators is advanced packaging, specifically CoWoS. Once I understood that, my conviction stopped wavering. Management put it plainly on the Q2 call: “Our packaging capacity is so tight that now it’s a little bit of my customers’ growth.” That is a foundry telling you demand exceeds what it can physically ship, and the constraint sits in the substrate and interposer step between the die and the board, not in the transistors themselves. Every leading AI accelerator on the market flows through this bottleneck, and TSMC owns it. The financials confirm the pricing power that comes with a chokepoint. In Q2 2026, TSMC posted EPS of $4.31 against a $3.8866 estimate, a 10.89% beat, on revenue of $40.2 billion, up 36.0% year over year. Gross margin came in at 67.7%, up 9.1 percentage points year over year. Advanced nodes at 7nm and below made up 77% of wafer revenue, with 3nm at 30%, 5nm at 33%, and 2nm debuting at 3% in its first commercial quarter. Then August monthly revenue landed up 53.3% year over year, and management raised full-year 2026 growth guidance to “slightly above 40% year-over-year in U.S. dollar terms.” The obvious alternatives get reached for first, and I have passed on each. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) is an integrated device maker that has repeatedly missed on leading-edge execution while TSMC ships 305 distinct process technologies and debuted A13 at the 2026 North America Technology Symposium. GlobalFoundries (NASDAQ:GFS) is a trailing-edge foundry with no sub-7nm exposure, meaning it does not compete for the wafer mix that generated 77% of TSMC’s revenue. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) sits on the customer side of this relationship, with a product that exists only because TSMC’s fabs and CoWoS capacity exist. Owning the toll road appeals to me more than owning one truck on it, especially when TSM trades at a forward P/E of 20 and a PEG of 0.816. Geographic concentration in Taiwan is real. Any escalation in cross-strait tension could interrupt production the market cannot easily replace. The 2nm ramp also carries near-term cost pressure. Management guided that the steep 2nm ramp will dilute Q3 gross margin by about 3 to 4 percentage points. What has not changed my thesis: the additional $100 billion U.S. investment and total Arizona commitment cited at $265 billion spread the geographic risk, and the margin dilution is investment-phase spending against demand management calls “stronger and stronger and stronger.” TSMC is guiding to a 2024 to 2029 revenue CAGR approaching 25% in USD and a long-term gross margin above 56%, holds $110 billion in cash and marketable securities, and told investors to expect “a continued and increasing cash dividends per share in 2027 as well.” The stock is already up 60.06% over the past year and 270.13% over five, and the thesis still holds. When the world’s AI build-out has to pass through one company’s back-end capacity, I want to own that company for the next decade (and the power, cooling, and networking suppliers feeding those fabs are worth a look too, which is why we pulled seven of them into a free AI infrastructure report). title: Museum Closed, Cars for Sale: Here's What Happened - Amarillo Country Radio
content: One gem on Route 66 sits in a truck stop on I-40 in Glenrio, NM. It is Russell's Travel Center Museum. The museum is full of classic cars, classic motorcycles, classic gas station signs, fuel pumps, and a ton of nostalgia. Or should I say, was full of all those amazing things. Unfortunately, the museum is now closed and empty. One of the not-so-great things about social media is running across something that makes you sad during your doomscrolling. That's exactly what happened to me. I was scrolling, and I saw a car on an auction site, then another, and I realized they were cars from Russell's Travel Center Museum. Read More: Road Trip To An Amazing Car Museum on Route 66 Now the museum is closed, and the days of Russell's Travel Center are gone. According to Truckers News, TravelCenters of America (TA) purchased the truck stop at 1583 Frontage Rd 4132 in 2023. Route 66 News reported that as part of the TA sale, the Russell's Travel Center name would remain for three years. Now that the three years are up, the travel center has been officially rebranded as TA, and the contents of the free museum were removed in July 2026. Even though the museum was free, it did have a donation box. Over 15 years, $520,000 was donated to food banks in Amarillo and Tucumcari. Assiter Auctioneers is holding an online auction with 432 lots from Russell's. The auction ends on October 10, 2026. The auction preview will be Thursday, October 8, and Friday, October 9, from 9 am to 5 pm. Vehicles may be previewed at the Assiter Auction Facility at 16650 I-27 in Canyon. The other items may be previewed at the museum inside the truck stop. The museum contained many historical and collector items. There were gas station signs like Texaco and Gulf, and the classic pumps that once filled those cars. Inside, there were vintage traffic lights, street signs, movie and music memorabilia, and of course, the classic cars. The cars at the start of the auction have very low bids. However, by the time the auction closes, these beauties from yesteryear will likely go for tens of thousands of dollars. I'm sad. It was a traditional stop when my family and I traveled into New Mexico. When my husband and I first started dating, we got in the car, and I started driving. I didn't tell him where we were going; I just went west on I-40. It freaked him out a little bit, not knowing where I was taking him. I knew he liked classic cars, and it was the perfect surprise date destination. I took him to the museum, and then we had breakfast at the diner. I'm sure it was a tradition for many people. If you have the funds and the means, you can now own a piece of this museum. Read More: Glenrio, Texas; The Ghost Town That's Coming Back To Life The truck stop is still there; however, it is no longer Russell's Travel Center. It is now a TA. The museum is what made the truck stop special, and now that it's gone, it's just another stop for fuel, snacks, and a potty break.
